title: Rotation Matrix <-> Quaternion (by hand)
hints: The trace gives w: tr(R) = 4w² − 1. The off-diagonal differences give x, y, z: R(2,1) − R(1,2) = 4wx, etc.

That divides by 4w, which blows up for 180° rotations (trace = −1, w = 0). If the trace is ≤ 0, use the largest diagonal element instead (Shepperd's method): e.g. x = ½√(1 + R00 − R11 − R22), then w, y, z from sums/differences of off-diagonals divided by 4x.
quatToRot: normalize q first, then use the standard formula, e.g. R(0,0) = 1 − 2(y² + z²), R(0,1) = 2(xy − wz).
Canonicalize the output: if w < 0, negate the whole quaternion.
